# netskope_gre_tunnel (Data Source)

GRE (Generic Routing Encapsulation) tunnels provide connectivity between your
network infrastructure and the Netskope cloud. GRE tunnels encapsulate traffic
and route it through Netskope's security services.

This resource supports full CRUD operations for managing GRE tunnel configurations.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "netskope_gre_tunnel" "my_gretunnel" {
  tunnel_id = 0
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `tunnel_id` (Number) Unique identifier for the GRE tunnel (assigned by API)

### Read-Only

- `bandwidth` (Number) Bandwidth limit in Mbps (default 1000)
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the tunnel is enabled
- `notes` (String) User-provided notes or description for the tunnel
- `options` (Attributes) Advanced tunnel options (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--options))
- `site` (String) Site name for the tunnel - used to identify the tunnel location
- `source_ip` (String) Source IP address identity - the public IP of your GRE tunnel endpoint
- `source_type` (String) Source device type
- `template` (String) Configuration template name
- `vendor` (String) Network equipment vendor name (e.g., Cisco, Palo Alto, Fortinet)

<a id="nestedatt--options"></a>
### Nested Schema for `options`

Read-Only:

- `xff` (Attributes) X-Forwarded-For header configuration (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--options--xff))

<a id="nestedatt--options--xff"></a>
### Nested Schema for `options.xff`

Read-Only:

- `xff_enabled` (Boolean) Enable X-Forwarded-For header insertion
- `xff_ip_list` (List of String) List of IP addresses for XFF header
